semantically_equivalent_models.justification: "lda" is a common abbreviation for "Linear Discriminant Analysis", and thus they are semantically equivalent.

parent_models.justification: Support Vector Machines (SVMs) and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) are both linear classification methods under the broader category of discriminant analysis techniques.
The Support Vector Classifier is part of the Support Vector Machines family which, like LDA, involves linear classification methods.

closest_parent_model.justification: Support Vector Machines (SVMs) broadly encompass Linear Discriminant Analysis as they are both linear classifiers and share a closer relation at a high level as methods for boundary classification.

child_models.justification: Partial Least-Squares Discriminant Analysis extends the concept of Linear Discriminant Analysis by incorporating the Partial Least Squares approach to handle multicollinearity and high dimensionality.
LDCQ is a variation that builds on LDA principles, potentially making it a more specific variant.

closest_child_model.justification: Partial Least-Squares Discriminant Analysis extends the concept of LDA more directly by marrying it with PLS, making it a specific form or extension of linear discriminant techniques.

sibling_models.justification: Support Vector Classifier can be seen as a sibling model, as both it and LDA are part of the broader class of discriminant analysis, focusing on classification.

sibling_models.value: support vector machine with linear kernel
sibling_models.justification: SVM with a linear kernel is closely related to LDA as both employ linear decision boundaries for classification.
Similar to Support Vector Machine with a linear kernel, this variant also falls under the same broader category of linear classifiers as LDA.

closest_sibling_model.justification: Support Vector Classifier is the most similar in terms of function and purpose to LDA, as both are functional classifiers focusing on decision boundaries.

unrelated_models.justification: Canonical correlation analysis is used for multivariable data correlation and doesn't directly relate to discriminant analysis or linear classification methods like LDA.
